The relevant excerpt of the impugned order is reproduced as under for ready reference:-
"....
It is settled law that at the stage of framing of charges, a prima-facie case has to be seen to be made out against the accused persons and no roving enquiry is needed.
In the present case, there are clear allegations against accused no. 3, the mother-in-law of the complainant.
However, there are no clear allegations against the accused no. 2 father-in-law of the complainant.

She has simply mentioned "sasural wale"
while imputing criminality upon the conduct of the accused persons, however, such vague and general allegations cannot suffice as a prima facie case being made out against accused no. 2 as he has not been specifically mentioned by name by the complainant anywhere in the said complaint.
Therefore, in light of absence of any allegations against accused no. 2, he is discharged of the offences under Section 498-A/406/34 IPC in the present case.

sentences.text: 9. The scope of interference in a revision petition is extremely narrow.

It is well settled that Section 397 CrPC gives the High Courts or the Sessions Courts jurisdiction to consider the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding inter se an order and as to the regularity of the proceedings of any inferior court.

It is also well settled that while considering the legality, propriety or correctness of a finding or a conclusion, normally the revising court does not dwell at length upon the facts and evidence of the case.

A court in revision considers the material only to satisfy itself about the legality and propriety of the findings, sentence and order and refrains from substituting its own conclusion on an elaborate consideration of evidence...."

sentences.text:
It is argued by Ld. Counsel for petitioners that the respondent no. 2 had used term "sasural wale"
in her complaint in vague manner and it cannot be ascertained as to whom she was actually referring to while levelling the allegations.
It is further argued that Ld. Trial Court discharged father in law i.e. accused no. 2 of all the alleged offences on this ground alone.
As such, the present petitioners are also entitled to the discharged on the grounds of parity.

13. This argument though lacks merit as the names of each of the accused persons had been clearly mentioned by the complainant in the subject of the complaint dated 02.09.2017 and in paragraph no. 3 of her complaint, she referred to all the accused persons as mentioned above.

No doubt, the complainant should have ascribed specific roles to each accused persons while levelling allegations against each of them, however, a layman cannot be expected to know the nitty gritties of law at the time of filing a complaint.

Merely, the fact that father-in-law i.e. accused no. 2 got benefit of doubt in the absence of any specific allegation against him does not mean that the other accused persons i.e. mother-in-law and sister-in-law would also be afforded the same benefit.

In addition to the general allegations levelled against all the accused as mentioned above, specific allegations have also been levelled against sister-in-law i.e. petitioner no. 2 that she used to torture and harass respondent no.

The relevant observations are as under:-
"....

Taking note of the exposition of law on the subject laid down by this Court, it is settled that the Judge while considering the question of framing charge under Section 227 CrPC in sessions cases(which is akin to Section 239 CrPC pertaining to warrant cases) has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been Nasreen Akhtar vs State on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32191487/
6 made out; where the material placed before the Court discloses grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained, the Court will be fully justified in framing the charge

; by and large if two views are possible and one of them giving rise to suspicion only, as distinguished from grave suspicion against the accused, the trial Judge will be justified in discharging him.
It is thus clear that while examining the discharge application filed under Section 227 CrPC, it is expected from the trial Judge to exercise its judicial mind out or not.
It is true that in such proceedings, the Court is not supposed to hold a mini trial by marshalling the evidence on record...."

15.

Furthermore, in the case of Bhawna Bai v. Ghanshyam, (2020) 2 SCC 217, Hon'ble Apex Court had held that:-
"....
At the time of framing the charges, only prima facie case is to be seen; whether case is beyond reasonable doubt, is not to be seen at this stage.
At the stage of framing the charge, the court has to see if there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
While evaluating the materials, strict standard of proof is not required; only prima facie case against the accused is to be seen...."
16. Thus, that at the stage of framing of charge, only prima-facie case is to be seen, whether case is beyond reasonable doubt, is not to be seen.
Further, court is not supposed to hold a mini trial by marshalling the evidence on record at this stage.

17. In view of material on record, specific complaint of complainant/ respondent no. 2 and statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. of other witnesses, Ld. Trial Court was justified in framing prima facie charges against accused persons namely Sayyed Asim Pasha, Nasreen Akhtar (petitioner no. 1 herein) and Nausheen Fatima (petitioner no. 2 herein) for the offences under Section 498-A/34 IPC.
18.
With these observations, it is held that there is no infirmity/ patent illegality or jurisdictional error in the impugned order dated 06.07.2022.
Accordingly, the revision petition stands dismissed.

Trial Court was justified in framing prima facie charges against accused persons namely Sayyed Asim Pasha, Nasreen Akhtar (petitioner no. 1 herein) and Nausheen Fatima (petitioner no. 2 herein) for the offences under Section 498-A/34 IPC.
18.
With these observations, it is held that there is no infirmity/ patent illegality or jurisdictional error in the impugned order dated 06.07.2022.
